item.title: Gilead Arthritis Drug Failure
item.description:
• Summary: Gilead Sciences has scrapped its lead arthritis drug, acquired through the $405 million buyout of MiroBio, after disappointing clinical results. The candidate was a BTLA-targeted therapy for rheumatoid arthritis. The failure is a setback for the BTLA pathway in autoimmune diseases.
  • MoAs: BTLA (B- and T-lymphocyte attenuator) agonist; activates BTLA receptor to inhibit T-cell activation and reduce autoimmune inflammation.
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech
